prose.summary: The sweet biscuits meet the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate (the reduced rate under the trade agreement) of 0% can be claimed instead of the normal 30% duty. This results in an estimated saving of 8100.00 USD. Follow the checklist below to claim the preference.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 19053100, Sweet biscuits, with high confidence. You should confirm this code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal MFN rate (the normal import duty rate) is 30% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 8100.00 USD.
prose.origin: The rule of origin is CTH plus VA 40%, which means each non‑originating input must be classified in a different 4‑digit heading and the value addition must be at least 40% on an FOB basis (the price of the goods loaded on board at the UAE port). All required checks passed: final manufacture in the UAE, work beyond minimal operations, all three non‑originating inputs are outside heading 1905, and the value addition is 55.0% against the 40% threshold.

notes.text: Fees are calculated in AED based on the invoice value in AED; Mansha does not convert currencies.
For a retrospective certificate, the agreement specifies box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's form uses box 9; follow India's form.
India's tariff schedule marks this 30% rate with a footnote that Mansha has not checked; confirm the normal (MFN) rate with Indian customs or a customs broker.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

Only for a certificate issued retrospectively: the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
